c.tagline: Africa's smallest capital, where granite hills meet turquoise sea.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are set by government-regulated fixed zones/routes rather than meters; agree the price with the driver before departure, especially from the airport.

emergency.note: 999 is the national police emergency line; 151 reaches the ambulance/SAMU service at Victoria Hospital. 112 works as a general emergency number from mobiles.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty theft from beaches, cars and unattended bags occurs; skip unlit backstreets and quiet beaches after dark.

hood_desc: The compact capital's core around the clock tower, market and Independence Avenue; walkable, historic, and convenient for banking, ferries and day trips, suited to first-timers who want an urban base.
Mahé's most popular beach strip, 5km northwest of town, lined with restaurants, bars and dive shops; suits travelers who want beach access with nightlife and easy bus links to Victoria.

A manmade marina island of canals and waterfront apartments just off the east coast, close to the airport; suits couples and families wanting a resort-like, self-catering base with restaurants and a casino.

Quieter north-coast stretch of granite coves below Glacis hill, home to upscale resorts and calm bays; suits honeymooners and travelers seeking a peaceful, scenic retreat with easy access to Beau Vallon.
A laid-back south-coast district of small bays, local eateries and modest guesthouses; suits budget travelers and those wanting an authentic, low-key Seychellois village feel away from the crowds.

water.note: Technically meets WHO standards, but official tourism advice recommends bottled water due to chlorination.

transit.pay: Pay the flat fare in cash (SCR) directly to the driver or conductor when boarding; there is no rechargeable transit card. Exact change is appreciated. Tourists typically pay the same flat fare as locals.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:30am-7:30pm on most routes with reduced frequency on Sundays; there is no late-night bus service, so taxis or pre-arranged transport are needed after dark.
transit.note: Victoria's small bus terminal is the hub for all Mahé routes; buses are inexpensive (under SCR 10 per ride) but infrequent, so many visitors rely on rental cars or taxis to explore beyond town.

transit.m: SPTC bus route from airport terminal to Victoria (approx. 20-30 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a 10% service charge is often already added at restaurants and resorts. Rounding up for taxis and small tips for good service are appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Victoria Clock Tower (Lorlorz)
This miniature replica of London's Little Ben stands at the city's central crossroads and is the most photographed symbol of the world's smallest capital.
Sir Selwyn Selwyn-Clarke Market
A bustling covered market bursting with tropical fruit, spices, and fresh fish, offering visitors a vivid, aromatic slice of everyday Seychellois life.
Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
This striking twin-towered Catholic cathedral, dating to the 19th century, anchors Victoria's skyline with its pale facade and ornate interior.
National Museum of History
Housed in a colonial-era building, this museum traces Seychelles' journey from pirate hideout to independent nation through compelling artifacts.
Arul Mihu Navasakthi Vinayagar Temple
A vividly painted Hindu temple with an intricately sculpted gopuram tower, its colorful facade making it one of the city's most photogenic landmarks.
Victoria Botanical Gardens
Lush gardens home to giant Aldabra tortoises, fruit bats, and rare coco de mer palms, offering a peaceful escape into Seychelles' unique biodiversity.
Victoria Harbour (Port Victoria)
The palm-fringed working harbor where fishing boats, yachts, and cargo ships mingle against a backdrop of granite mountains rising steeply behind town.
State House
The elegant colonial residence of the Seychellois president, fronted by manicured lawns and gates that make for an elegant architectural photo stop.
Independence Avenue
Victoria's main thoroughfare lined with colonial-era shopfronts and the historic Pirates Arms cafe, capturing the pulse of the capital's daily life.
Bicentennial Monument (Twa Zwazo)
This distinctive three-winged sculpture symbolizing the continents of Seychelles' settlers has become an iconic roundabout landmark near the harbor.

train.note: Seychelles has no railway. On Mahe, get around by the SPTC public buses, taxi or hire car.

bus.note: Being an island nation there are no international bus routes. Local buses on Mahe (and Praslin) are run by the state Seychelles Public Transport Corporation (SPTC), https://www.sptc.sc/.

intl.to: No international ferry - inter-island only (Mahe <> Praslin <> La Digue)

ferry.note: There are no international passenger ferries. Fast catamaran ferries link the main islands from the Inter Island Quay in Victoria: Cat Cocos (Mahe-Praslin-La Digue) at catcocos.com, plus the smaller Cat Rose service. Book ahead in peak season.

half.name: Beau Vallon Beach
half.blurb: Beau Vallon is Mahe's most popular beach, a curved stretch of sand on the island's northwest coast.

half.name: Sainte Anne Marine National Park
half.blurb: Sainte Anne Marine National Park protects a cluster of islands and coral reefs reached by boat from Victoria's harbor.

full.name: Praslin Island
full.blurb: Praslin is reached by ferry from Mahe and holds the Vallee de Mai, a UNESCO palm forest with the rare coco de mer.

full.name: La Digue Island
full.blurb: La Digue is a ferry ride from Mahe, known for granite boulder beaches like Anse Source d'Argent and ox-cart transport.
